Looking at the first fold: the strip makes angle α = 63° with crease AB. Reflecting the upper part across AB sends the strip's direction from (cos 63°, sin 63°) to (cos 63°, −sin 63°), producing the two arms of the middle figure.

For the second fold, the crease runs along the line through B and V (parallel to the original strip direction, i.e., along (cos 63°, sin 63°)). Reflecting the right arm's direction (cos 63°, −sin 63°) across this line gives:

v' = 2(v·w)w − v, where v·w = cos²63° − sin²63° = cos 126°.

This yields v' ≈ (−0.988, −0.157), the nearly horizontal arm in the final figure.

The angle β between this folded arm (v') and the remaining arm along (−cos 63°, −sin 63°) satisfies:

cos β = v'·d₁ = 0.588 → β = 54°.

Equivalently, β = 180° − 2α = 180° − 126° = 54°.

\boxed{D}
